message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 201, "amount_cents": 3873}, {"order_id": 203, "amount_cents": 18687}, {"order_id": 204, "amount_cents": 11000}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, since the handoff is only a claim. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.

The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 201, 203, 204 with the same amounts). Next I'll list the orders to check that each refund maps to a real order before relying on net_balance.
The refund list matches Alpha's handoff, and each refund maps to a real order without exceeding its amount. Next I'll get acme's net balance from the ledger rather than computing it myself.

I checked acme's figure against the order and refund lists: orders 200 (39447) and 203 (33625) minus refund 203 (18687) gives 54385, which matches net_balance. The refunds are consistent with the orders, so I'll record acme's payout now.
Acme's payout is recorded and matches the ledger. Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance, rather than computing it myself, before recording its payout.
Birch's net_balance of 29147 matches my check: orders 201 (4135) and 204 (39885) total 44020, minus refunds 201 (3873) and 204 (11000) gives 29147. I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt is the only customer left. Cobalt has orders 202 and 205 and no refunds, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance before recording the payout.
Cobalt's orders 202 (30107) and 205 (2972) total 33079 with no refunds, which matches net_balance. All three customers are now verified, so I'll record cobalt's payout.
All three customers have been paid. Each figure matched my own check against the orders and refunds, and every record_payout returned ok, so the batch is complete.
